arguments.command:
cat > /workspace/submission/README.md <<'EOF'
# Campaign extension workspace

`campaign.py` is the scored entry point. It reads one UTF-8 JSON campaign
object on stdin and writes one JSON result object on stdout; diagnostics
belong on stderr. Run it as `python3 -I -B campaign.py` so the module
directory and the sibling `../deps` are added to `sys.path` by the script
itself.

## Modules

* `common.py` - shared wire types: metadata validation, documentation
  address/prefix parsing, base64, JSON envelope rules and quota forests.
* `gen_targets.py` - expands leases into canary and low-IID /128 targets.
  The canary IID is `SHA256(seed \n lease_id \n canonical_/64)[:8] big
  endian | 2**63`. `plan()` returns the manifest, the numeric probe lookup
  and each lease's planned low targets. The legacy CLI still writes a
  target file.
* `classify_responses.py` - capture transport: base64 chunk decoding,
  Zstandard framing validation (complete, dictionary-free, bounded window,
  skippable and concatenated frames allowed, reserved bit rejected,
  truncation and checksum errors rejected) and the strict Excel CSV stream.
  `capture_records()` returns validated logical records plus the
  `[capture, ordinal]` rejection indices. The legacy CLI still emits
  network JSON lines.
* `ledger.py` - typed record parsing (`parse_record`) and revision-aware
  reconciliation (`Ledger.at`). The identity of a record is `(type,id)`
  across captures; the highest visible revision wins, identical semantic
  contents collapse (publication time, address spelling, decimal spelling
  and base64 spelling are ignored) and conflicting contents contribute no
  live record.
* `census.py` - per-query snapshots: lease states (`inactive`, `alias`,
  `conflict`, `usable`), raw conflicts, clean internal/external roles,
  earliest causal witnesses, unresolved low targets, the causal
  application census with per-service open/closed/unknown subsets and
  protocol error counts, and the frozen request activity table.
* `protocols.py` - offline ADB and usbmuxd sync wire validation plus the
  probe certificate packets. Nothing is ever transmitted.
* `planning.py` - the optimal quota-constrained follow-up plan.

## Planning model

Every feasible assignment is one unit of flow: source, down the request
quota forest (a unit at the request's group and every ancestor), across
exactly one request/offer pair edge, up the offer quota forest (a unit at
the offer's group and every ancestor), sink. Each subtree constraint is an
aggregate over the requests or offers inside that subtree, so routing the
request side from the root downwards and the offer side from the offers
upwards makes integral flows correspond exactly to feasible assignments.
Cost sits only on the pair edges, so a min-cost maximum flow yields a
maximum-cardinality plan of minimum total offer cost. Interchangeable
requests (same quota group and same allowed offer set) and duplicate
offers (same allowed request set, group and cost) are merged first, and
quota nodes whose capacity can never bind are contracted.

## Legacy tools

`gen_targets.py` and `classify_responses.py` keep their original
command-line interfaces for development; they do not define the version 3
semantics, which live in PROTOCOL.md outside this directory.
EOF
cd /workspace && python3 -m py_compile submission/*.py && echo "compile ok" && ls submission/
